April 9
Allison Mann & Blue Plate Special — Monthly gig at Julio’s Cantina. 5-7 p.m. Julio’s Cantina, 54 State St., Montpelier. 802-229-9348.
Celebrate Local News! — Screening of “Reimagining Local News,” review of Vermont News and Information Ecosystem Research and panel discussion that explores how Vermont communities can strengthen trusted local news. 5:45-8 p.m. Kellogg-Hubbard Library, 135 Main St., Montpelier.
April 10
All That We Hold: Pop-up Exhibition — Join us to explore and reflect on the stories from our sisters, friends, children and neighbors. 6-8 p.m. The Phoenix Gallery & Music Hall, 5 Stowe St., Waterbury. 802-476-1388.
Tiny Glass Tavern presents: On and Ever Onward — Early music, Bulgarian, Swedish & American folk, pop, originals, and more. 7-9 p.m. Unitarian Church of Montpelier, 130 Main St., Montpelier. 857-205-5266.
Art Gallery Reception: A Critical Balance — Join a group of Vermont and New Hampshire artists working with Biodiversity Research Institute to highlight the endangered birds of Amboseli Park in Kenya 5 to 7 p.m., 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
April 11
Vermont Woodlands Association Annual Conference — VWA will host the 2026 conference at Vermont State University in Randolph. 8:45-4 p.m. Vermont State University Randolph Campus, 124 Admin Drive, Randolph.
Montpelier Community Spruce Up Day — A community event to tidy and beautify downtown Montpelier. 11-2 p.m. 39 Main St., Montpelier. 802-223-9604.
2026 Mud Season Variety Show — Produced by The Chandler Players, it celebrates local talent and community spirit, 6-9 p.m. Chandler Music Hall, 71 North Main St., Randolph. 802-728-9878.
New England K9 Search and Rescue Demonstration — An informational presentation with a live search demonstration with the dogs, 11 to noon. Philo Ridge Farm, 2766 Mount Philo Road, Charlotte. 603-526-6754.
Waterbury LEAP Energy Fair — 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Crossett Brook Middle School, 5672 Vermont Route 100, Duxbury. 802-244-1293.
Brain Injury Support Group — Noon-1 p.m. Aldrich Public Library, 6 Washington St., Barre. 802-558-4428.
2026 Infusion Fashions: A Chemo Gown Extravaganza — Join us for a one-of-a-kind event where the infusion nurses at UVM Medical Center showcase creative outfits made from chemo gowns to benefit American Cancer Society 5-8:30 p.m. DoubleTree by Hilton Burlington Vermont, 870 Williston Road, South Burlington. 802-257-6719.
April 12
Green Mountain Youth Symphony Spring Concert — 2-4 p.m. Barre Opera House, 6 North Main St., Barre.
MakerSphere Open House — Demonstrations in clay, stained glass and woodworking. Exhibit of students’ work. 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. 201 Hollow Road, Waterbury.
Dance, Sing, and Jump Around — Movers and shakers of all ages learn traditional circle and line dances and singing games 3 to 4:30 pm. Capital City Grange, 6612 Vermont 12, Berlin. 802-223-1509.
April 13
BFA Exhibit — Exhibit and artist talk at the Julian Scott Memorial Gallery on the VTSU-Johnson campus. 9-5 p.m. Vermont State University Johnson Campus, 337 College Hill Road, Johnson. 802-635-1469.
April 15
Central VT OLLI — Risqué and Revealing: Cinema of the Early 1930s with Rick Winston, 1:30-3 p.m. Savoy Theatre, 26 Main St., Montpelier.
Freedom to Read Panel Discussion — Engaging and timely conversation on the state of intellectual freedom in the United States. 6-7:30 p.m. St. Johnsbury Athenaeum, 1171 Main St., Saint Johnsbury. 802-748-8291.
After the Dams: A Community Conversation on Dam Removal, Flood Resilience, and River Recreation — Presentations and conversations about how to transform Montpelier's rivers through dam removals, flood resilience projects, and in-river recreation. 6-8 p.m. 58 Barre St., Montpelier.
A Dark and Starry Night: Why and How to Preserve Dark Skies in Vermont — 7-9 p.m., 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Robin’s Nest Nature Playgroup — A free activity for families to gather, learn, and play in nature. 10 a.m.-noon. 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Central VT OLLI — “Three on a Match” (1932 film), with Rick Winston; 1:30 to 3 p.m. Savoy Theatre, 26 Main St., Montpelier. 802-223-5886.
April 16
Jazz Pianist David Childs in Concert — A playful, spontaneous jazz performance of well-known classics and standards. 6:30-8 p.m. St. Johnsbury Athenaeum, 1171 Main St. 802-748-8291.
April 17
Music in the Gallery Concert Series — Musician Tom Stamp. 1-2 p.m. St. Johnsbury Athenaeum, 1171 Main St., Saint Johnsbury. 802-748-8291.
April 18
Friction Fire Skills Circle for Teens — Carve your own friction fire kit. Noon-3 p.m. 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Earth Day Celebration and Solidarity Art Build — Hosted by Families Rise Up and 350VT, community singing, face painting, snacks, T-shirt printing, and sign-making. 10 a.m. to noon. State Capitol, 115 State St., Montpelier.
Henna Adornment with Mary Numme at Studio Place Arts — 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., 201 North Main St., Barre. 802-479-7069.
Bringing Up Beaver — Licensed volunteer wildlife rehabilitator John Aberth presents on his book. 10-11 a.m. St. Johnsbury Athenaeum, 1171 Main St. 802-748-8291.
Spring Farmers Market — A market of farmer, growers, bakers, artists and craftsmen 9 a.m.-1 p.m. Vermont State University Randolph Campus, 124 Admin Drive, Randolph.
Laurel Canyon — The Ultimate Crosby Stills, Nash and Young Tribute Band. Experience Laurel Canyon, an acoustic trio of celebrated singers honoring Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young with definitive tributes to their hits, early bands, and solo years. 7-9 p.m. Chandler Center for the Arts, 71 North Main St., Randolph. 802-728-9878.
April 19
Opera Company of Middlebury’s Youth Opera Program presents: Una Giornata! — Students from across Vermont perform in an original opera consisting of all 24 Italian songs and arias. Stage directed by Sarah Cullins and music directed by Mary Jane Austin. 2-3 p.m. Montpelier Performing Arts Hub, 35 College St., Montpelier.
VT Symphony Jukebox: Porch Songs — Americana Roots, 5-6:30 p.m., Barre Opera House, 6 N Main St., Barre. 802-864-5741.

"The Librarians" Free Film Screening with Indie Lens Pop-Up (preregister) — 6-7:30 p.m. St. Johnsbury Athenaeum, 1171 Main St., Saint Johnsbury. 802-748-8291.
Bela Fleck’s BEATrio — Bela Fleck teams with Edmar Castaneda and Antonio Sanchez for a genre-blurring trio. 7-9 p.m. Chandler Center for the Arts, 71 North Main St., Randolph. 802-728-9878.

Muddy Onion Gravel Grinder — The classic Central Vermont spring gravel grinder with after party on Montpelier's MudFest weekend. 7-4 p.m. 89 Main St., Montpelier. 802-225-6736.
Montpelier MudFest — A weekend-long celebration of Vermont's iconic mud season, happening April 25-26. 8:30-10 p.m. Montpelier.
Earth Day Tree Planting — Third annual Earth Day tree planting event. 10 a.m.-1 p.m. 713 Elm St., Montpelier. 802-229-6206.
Author Christy Mihaly visits Inklings Children's Books — Mihaly will read from her new book, "Music and Silence: The Passion and Protest of Pablo Casals." 11-noon. 106 Mad River Green, Waitsfield. 802-496-7280.
Brain Injury Support Group — Noon-1 p.m. Aldrich Public Library, 6 Washington St., Barre. 802-558-4428.
Bloom Flower and Home Market — Celebrate the start of spring by shopping from vendors of indoor and outdoor plants, home decor, art, and more at Hula! 12-6 p.m. Hula, 50 Lakeside Avenue, Burlington.
Capital City Concerts presents a Faure Foray — Violinist Laurie Smukler returns with New York City colleagues Tal First, Natasha Brofsky and Qing Jiang for an all-Faure evening. 7:30-9 p.m. Unitarian Church of Montpelier, 130 Main St., Montpelier.
April 26
Montpelier MudFest — A weekend-long celebration of Vermont's iconic mud season, happening April 25-26. Montpelier.
The Mucker 2026 — Bring your energy outdoors into the mud and fresh air at The Mucker, part of Montpelier MudFest. 9-11 a.m. Vermont State House/Hubbard Park, 115 State St., Montpelier.
Shaun Booher — Live organ concert. Proceeds to benefit Vermont Interfaith Action’s vital work. 3-4 p.m. Unitarian Church of Montpelier, 130 Main St., Montpelier.

PoemTown St. Johnsbury Reading and Reception — Twelve poets from the more than 100 who submit poems this year will share their poems at this year's PoemTown St. Johnsbury Reading and Reception. 6:30-9:30 p.m. St. Johnsbury Athenaeum, 1171 Main St. 802-748-8291.

Bookstock 2026 — Vermont Festival of Words, features author readings; used book sale; poetry; workshops; events for children; food; and other festivities centered on Woodstock’s Green. 1 to 3 p.m. The Green, Woodstock. 802-432-8182.
From Doing to Being: Resting as a Path to Liberation — Come relax, rest, and restore while deepening your understanding on your path to liberation.Free. 5 p.m. Adamant Music School, 1216 Haggett Road, Calais. 802-825-1815.

Green Mountain Youth Symphony 25th Anniversary Celebration — 25 years of classical music education and community in central Vermont, 4-7 p.m. Montpelier Performing Arts Hub Chapel Hall, 36 College St., Montpelier.
